pathway.claim: p.Leu737Ter allele: transcript predicted NMD-degraded (PTC ~750 nt upstream of last junction); any escaped product lacks the kinase-like domain. p.Asn1002Lys allele: full-length protein with a destabilising substitution in the pseudokinase domain.
Cellular BubR1 abundance falls towards a single partially-functional allele's output; >50% loss of BubR1 expression/activity is sufficient for the PCS/MVA phenotype.
Low BubR1 weakens the spindle-assembly checkpoint and reduces KARD-dependent PP2A-B56 recruitment that corrects kinetochore-microtubule attachment errors.
Uncorrected errors produce constitutional mosaic gains and losses of whole chromosomes - the defining feature of MVA1.
Aneuploid daughter cells arrest via p53/p21, acquire proteotoxic stress and senescence programmes (p16 effector), and signal for immune clearance.

Chronic aneuploidy plus senescence yields growth failure and progeroid decline, while rare escaping aneuploid clones drive childhood cancer (rhabdomyosarcoma, Wilms; adult GI cancers on milder genotypes).

claims.text: p.Leu737Ter (c.2210T>G) creates a premature termination codon in exon 17 of 23 of ENST00000287598 (MANE); the PTC lies 748 nt upstream of the last exon-exon junction, far beyond the 50-55 nt rule threshold, so the mutant transcript is predicted to be degraded by nonsense-mediated mRNA decay

If translated despite predicted NMD, the truncated product would carry only residues 1-736 (29.9% of the 1050-aa protein lost): the entire C-terminal kinase-like domain (UniProt 766-1050), the PLK1 phosphoacceptor sites T792/T1008, and the 772-780 binding region are absent, while the N-terminal KEN boxes, TPR, KNL1-binding (152-185), D-box (224-232), K250 acetylation site and KARD phospho-region (S670/S676) are retained - consistent with a null allele
p.Leu737Ter is ultra-rare in population data: gnomAD v4 exomes 115/1461846 alleles (AF 7.87e-05), genomes 5/152174 (AF 3.29e-05), 0 homozygotes - consistent with a deleterious germline allele
ClinVar records c.2210T>G (VCV000533901) as Pathogenic/Likely pathogenic for Mosaic variegated aneuploidy syndrome 1 (OMIM 257300), criteria provided, multiple submitters, no conflicts

p.Asn1002Lys (c.3006T>G, exon 23, the last exon) substitutes a positively charged Lys for a highly conserved Asn at residue 1002 inside the C-terminal kinase-like domain (766-1050), 6 residues from the PLK1 phosphosite T1008

Missense-effect predictors converge on deleterious for N1002K: AlphaMissense 0.9229 (likely_pathogenic), SIFT 0.01 (deleterious), PolyPhen-2 0.997 (probably_damaging), CADD_phred 24.5, phyloP 5.115; REVEL 0.472 is moderate and below the commonly used 0.5-0.75 supporting thresholds, stated honestly rather than overclaimed

On the AlphaFold O60566 model (v6), N1002 has pLDDT 91.06 and 27 residues within 8 A (all-atom; 8 by CA) - a partially packed surface region of the pseudokinase C-lobe (contact-number percentile 53.7% within the domain), so the Asn->Lys charge introduction plausibly perturbs local packing/stability rather than a catalytic centre

p.Asn1002Lys is absent from gnomAD v4 genomes and seen once in 1461878 exome alleles (AF 6.84e-07, 0 homozygotes); ClinVar has no entry for c.3006T>G itself, while the same protein change via c.3006T>A is a VUS (VCV004600147, single submitter) - the allele is novel to this child

MVA-patient missense alleles that map in or near the BUBR1 kinase domain characteristically produce unstable protein (high turnover), so N1002K is predicted to act as a hypomorph through reduced abundance; residual function is unmeasured in this child

The C-terminal pseudokinase domain where N1002 sits is required for KARD phosphorylation and PP2A-B56 recruitment to kinetochores, for spindle-checkpoint silencing and for chromosome alignment - so a stability- or fold-disrupting lesion in this domain weakens error correction even though BUBR1 catalytic activity itself is dispensable

In published biallelic MVA1 cases a missense allele pairs with a truncating allele - completely truncating genotypes are effectively unseen, consistent with lethality of full BUBR1 loss; the proband's stop + kinase-domain missense pair fits this pattern exactly

Roughly >50% reduction of BUBR1 expression or activity is sufficient to cause the PCS/MVA phenotype, and single-allele carriers show mild mitotic defects - the genotype here is expected to leave only the N1002K allele as the functional copy

MVA patient cells show impaired spindle-assembly checkpoint, chromosome-alignment defects and low overall BUBR1 abundance; ectopic BUBR1 rescues the checkpoint, proving segregation errors stem from BUBR1 dysfunction

Reduced BUBR1 weakens both its mitotic-checkpoint arm and its attachment-error-correction arm: the KARD domain recruits PP2A-B56 to kinetochores in a PLK1-phosphorylation-dependent manner to counter Aurora B and stabilise kinetochore-microtubule attachments

Chromosome mis-segregation in otherwise diploid cells triggers p53 accumulation and p21-dependent cell-cycle delay, limiting proliferation of aneuploid cells; loss of p53 permits aneuploid clones to expand

Cells that mis-segregate acquire complex karyotypes, proteotoxic stress and senescent features with pro-inflammatory signalling that flags them for immune clearance - senescence is a direct consequence of aneuploidy

BubR1-insufficient mice develop progressive aneuploidy plus progeroid phenotypes (short lifespan, dwarfism, lordokyphosis, cataracts, fat and skeletal-muscle loss), and p16Ink4a is an effector of the senescence - graded BubR1 reduction increases aneuploidy and senescence dose-dependently

BUBR1-insufficiency states are cancer-prone: biallelic carriers developed embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma in the original MVA families, Wilms tumour is reported in BUB1B PCS/MVA, and a homozygous hypomorphic allele produced adult gastrointestinal neoplasia - aneuploidy is the causal link

BubR1 abundance is pharmacologically tractable: SIRT2 keeps BubR1 K668 deacetylated and its decline with falling NAD+ drives age-related BubR1 loss; SIRT2 overexpression or NMN raises BubR1 in vivo, and K250 acetylation by PCAF stabilises BubR1 by blocking its ubiquitin-dependent degradation

Raising BubR1 is protective: sustained high-level expression in mice preserves genomic integrity, corrects checkpoint and attachment defects, reduces tumorigenesis even on aneuploidising backgrounds, and extends healthy lifespan

Clearing p16-positive senescent cells in BubR1 progeroid mice delayed onset of age-related pathologies in adipose tissue, skeletal muscle and eye, and late-life clearance attenuated established disorders - the senescence burden is modifiable

Aneuploid cancer cells are selectively vulnerable to spindle-checkpoint perturbation and to KIF18A loss (synthetic-lethal interaction) - a therapeutic window against aneuploid malignant clones but the opposite of what a child with constitutional mis-segregation should receive prophylactically

Growth-hormone treatment in chromosomal-breakage / DNA-repair-disorder children is flagged for careful evaluation owing to malignancy risk; a large French childhood-cancer-survivor cohort found no significant increase in second neoplasms on GH, so the contraindication is precautionary, not proven

p53 is protective in this context: it limits aneuploid-cell propagation and delays functional decline of muscle and fat in BubR1-insufficient mice - suppressing p53 would remove the brake on aneuploid clone expansion and worsen tissue decline

uncertainties.text: Phase is UNKNOWN in this child (0 spanning reads in Track 1). In-trans configuration is inferred from the MVA1 genotype pattern (null + hypomorph) and phenotype fit, not observed. Resolution: parental testing, targeted long-range PCR or long-read phasing.

p.Asn1002Lys residual function is unmeasured. Assays that would quantify it: patient-fibroblast BubR1 western blot (abundance), nocodazole-arrest timing (SAC competency), k-fibre stability / cold-stable microtubule assay, aneuploidy rate by FISH or single-cell DNA-seq.
NMD for p.Leu737Ter is a positional prediction, not a measured decay rate; NMD efficiency varies and rare escape could yield a 736-aa fragment of uncertain activity.
Predictor agreement is strong but not unanimous: REVEL 0.472 is below usual supporting thresholds and the ClinVar record for the same amino-acid change (c.3006T>A) is a single-submitter VUS.

therapeutic_implications.text: The missense allele is the only functional copy; raising its abundance/stability is disease-modifying. BubR1 levels are druggable: SIRT2/NAD+ maintains BubR1 (NMN or SIRT2 upregulation raises BubR1 in vivo), K250 acetylation blocks BubR1 degradation, and transgenic BubR1 overexpression corrects checkpoint defects, aneuploidy, tumorigenesis and progeroid decline.
Senescent-cell burden is a downstream driver of the growth/progeroid phenotype and is modifiable: p16 clearance in BubR1 progeroid mice delayed and attenuated tissue dysfunction.

Surviving aneuploid cells are the cancer substrate; immune clearance of complex karyotypes is part of natural control, and aneuploid tumour cells carry selective vulnerabilities (SAC dependency, KIF18A) relevant if malignancy arises.
Mechanism predicts childhood embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma and Wilms tumour risk plus later GI neoplasia - regular surveillance is mechanism-justified independent of any drug choice.

contraindications.text: Systemic weakening of an already-insufficient checkpoint increases mis-segregation and aneuploid-clone supply. Nuance: aneuploid CANCER cells are selectively killed by these agents - relevant to treating an established tumour, contraindicated as prophylaxis.
p53/p21 is the brake limiting propagation of aneuploid cells and protecting muscle/fat in BubR1-insufficient mice; lifting it expands aneuploid clones.

Guidance flags GH use in chromosomal-breakage / DNA-repair disorders for caution because of malignancy risk; in a constitutional-aneuploidy cancer-predisposition syndrome, accelerating clone expansion is mechanistically counterproductive. Counter-evidence: a large survivor cohort found no significant second-neoplasm increase, so this is precautionary.
Chronic spindle poisons / aneugens add mis-segregation on top of a constitutionally weak checkpoint - the opposite direction of the therapeutic goal.
